4. Pmblem Files 
4.3. Trajectory Data Blocks 
4.3.2. *Dwn/crs Data Block 
4.3.2. *Dwn/crs Data Block 
East, north, downrange, and crossrange are defrned from a reference point, given by 
a longitude and geodetic latitude, as shown in Figure 4-4. The trajectory is projected 
to the earth's surface, and the distances are measured along this curve (Section 2.4.1). 
East is the component of distance traveled along a constant latitude and north is the 
component of distance traveled along a constant longitude. Downrange is the com- 
ponent of distance traveled along a reference azimuth or heading, and crossrange is 
the component of distance traveled perpendicular to this heading. 
Point 
Figure U. 
Downrange and Crossrange Definition. 
All of these distances use the same reference point. The reference heading is only 
used by the downrange and crossrange calculations. The reference longitude, lati- 
tude, and heading default to the beginning of the trajectory given by the initial condi- 
tions. 
If adifferent reference point is required or if multiple trajectories need to use the same 
reference point, then these values can be given in the *dwdcrs data block. For exam- 
ple, 
*dwn/crs latgd=lO long=95 azm=45 
places the reference point at a latitude of 10°N and alongitude of 95'E. The reference 
heading or azimuth is 45' from north or northeast.
